spot.html_text: Much of Du Bos’s book is devoted to an explanation of artistic genius. He is particularly concerned to explain why certain eras (the Golden Age of Athens, the Rome of Augustus, the Italian Renaissance, and the era of Louis XIV) are more productive of geniuses. Although Du Bos says, in passing, that a “poet needs divine inspiration” (241), he decisively rejects the Platonic conception of genius. Instead, he believes that genius has physical causes.
